facts.fact: The World Bank's results framework for GALOP gives 733 schools assessing and reporting Differentiated Learning literacy and numeracy outcomes for individual learners on the DL+ Platform at 27 November 2025, against a target of 16,000 by December 2028; no total of schools is given.
The World Bank describes schools assessing and reporting literacy and numeracy outcomes for individual learners on the DL+ Platform, 733 schools doing so at 27 November 2025.

The Differentiated Learning programme whose outcomes schools report on the DL+ Platform is for lower and upper primary, with a further target of 35,000 primary teachers trained in it, per the World Bank at November 2025.

The count of schools reporting on the DL+ Platform stood at 733 in August 2024, on 20 June 2025 and on 27 November 2025; the World Bank says training of teachers to start reporting was delayed by the Ministry of Finance's disbursement cap in force from January 2025.

Schools reporting on the DL+ Platform is a performance-based condition carrying US$25 million under GALOP's second additional financing, which is grant-financed by GPE, SCALE funders and the Early Learning Partnership and had disbursed nothing by November 2025.
